description:
What happens when a musician with no formal science training helps NASA capture the first sounds ever recorded on Mars—and hears only silence? In this deeply human story, Jason Achilles traces a journey from childhood wonder to crushing failure to a breakthrough that traveled 127 million miles back to Earth. This talk celebrates curiosity, persistence, and how chasing the dreams that scare us most can change a life—and expand humanity’s sense of possibility. Jason Achilles bridges the worlds of music and space exploration. A Chicago-born composer and sonic innovator, he helped capture the first recorded sounds from Mars, transforming how humans connect with the cosmos through sound.

Inspired early by Prokofiev’s Peter and the Wolf, Vladimir Horowitz, and The Muppet Show, Jason developed a musical vision that reached beyond Earth. While earning his BA in Music at UC Berkeley, he composed Schizmatique No. 1 & 2, later recorded in Prague and Budapest and premiered at Carnegie Hall and S
title: The first sounds from Mars—recorded by a musician and NASA | Jason Achilles | TEDxManhattanBeach

description: More than 50 years since Americans last walked on the Moon and declared victory in the first space race with the Soviet Union, we’re once again hearing familiar language: race, competition, the Moon. But Sariah Fischer argues that Space Race 2.0 against China isn’t a sprint to a landing site; it’s a race to build permanence. Today’s “one small step” isn’t just a footprint or a flag, but an expanding industrial base combined with NASA, the Space Force, and our partners in the Artemis Accords to create a sustained presence—and a real chance to lead. Sariah Fischer works at the intersection of national security, commercial innovation, and humanity’s future in space. As Director of Business Development at Interlune, she is helping lay the foundation for a sustainable return to the Moon, starting with Helium-3. Her work centers on building the infrastructure and partnerships needed to support a lasting presence beyond Earth, aligning commercial momentum with the goals of NASA, the Departme
title: Space Race 2.0: Flags, footprints, and lunar permanence | Sariah Fischer | TEDxWakeForestU

description:
People rarely say what they actually mean—and that’s where the real story begins. As a songwriter, I’ve trained myself to listen for the motive behind the message, trusting that decoding others isn’t about judgment; it’s about curiosity, empathy, and reading between the lines of someone’s lived experience. The more honestly I learn to decode others, the more courage I have to rewrite my own story.
 MŌRIAH’s Mexican roots are evident in her work as an actress, producer (music & film), recording artist and songwriter. The L.A. native who now calls Nashville home, delivered her debut, “Hasta Mañana,” in English and Spanish in the Fall of 2024 and is part of CMT’s 2025 Next Women of Country class. In early 2025, she released her follow-up single “Sombrero” in English and Spanish and song’s music video debuted in Times Square in May. BILLBOARD has taken note of her “country sound and mariachi flair,” THE TENNESSEAN says she is “among the first to blend a strong Latin and mariachi influence
title: How to decode others without writing them off | MŌRIAH | TEDxNashvilleWomen

description: This talk explores how everyday actions, often dismissed as small, can empower others and create lasting change. It shows how positive action can break cycles of negativity and generate powerful ripple effects. Raimonds is a thoughtful and compassionate young speaker who is passionate about helping others recognise their value and potential. Drawing on the powerful metaphor of the “crab bucket,” his talk explores how self‑doubt, comparison, and negativity can hold people back — and how kindness, confidence, and encouragement can lift entire communities. Raimonds hopes to inspire others to break free from limiting beliefs, uplift those around them, and create positive ripples through everyday acts of empowerment. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: This talk tells the story of a young person’s journey through education. Through resilience and advocacy, it reveals how one courageous action can ripple outward and change the futures of others. Inioluwa is a courageous and resilient young advocate who has transformed personal hardship into powerful action. After facing repeated rejection while trying to secure a school place, she found her voice, spoke up for herself, and eventually addressed the Northern Ireland Assembly — a moment that ignited her passion for change. Using her experience to open doors for other young people who faced similar barriers, she demonstrates how one act of courage can spark a ripple effect of opportunity and hope. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: This is the story of a boy with a dream, an ambition to chase something greater. Sai Natth stands as a testament to this duality: when the known results with the unknown, we question whether it’s worth giving our all, and he answers that with an equation, the Equation of Becoming. Sai Natth is a Shell Scholar, eager to pursue Sustainable Engineering in the US, with the dream of developing renewable energy solutions for a cleaner future. Throughout high school, he learned to embrace failure, refine his skills, and push beyond limits. With 9A+ in SPM and accolades including Tokoh Kokurikulum and Olahragawan, he has set the bar higher than ever for his future endeavors. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: This talk sheds light on making small, intentional microchanges that restore balance, agency, and joy—allowing us to stay in our professions and thrive instead of wiping out. After experiencing burnout early in her primary care career, Dr. Diane Shannon left clinical practice to focus on writing and advocacy. For over 20 years, she has highlighted solutions to clinician burnout, system inefficiencies, and patient safety issues. She co-authored Preventing Physician Burnout: Curing the Chaos and Returning Joy to the Practice of Medicine (2016).Motivated by her own experience, she became a certified coach in 2019 and has since supported hundreds of clinicians in building sustainable, fulfilling careers. She launched her podcast, Vital Signs: Thriving as a Woman in Medicine, in January 2024 and continues to speak and write on clinician wellness. In her free time, she enjoys time with her three young adult children, traveling with her husband, and surfing. This talk was given at a TEDx eve
title: Riding the waves: Lessons from surfing to beat burnout | Diane Shannon | TEDxNortheasternU

title: Girls Like Me: Why Empowerment Isn’t Enough | Khushi Shah | TEDxNortheasternU

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk highlights how we can’t always avoid adversity, but we don’t have to remain impervious to it. What matters is how we respond, and whether that response allows us to grow. Rohan Venkatesh is a graduate of Northeastern University. He began his career in investment banking and private equity, following a carefully planned path after college. In 2021, shortly before relocating to New York City for his next role, he was diagnosed with brain cancer. Today, Rohan is a brain cancer survivor who is exploring how people respond to adversity and how those responses can lead to growth. This talk marks his first time sharing that journey on a public stage. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: When life doesn’t go back to normal | Rohan Venkatesh | TEDxNortheasternU

description: This talk peels back the layers and history of the US healthcare system as an urgent message to unite for reform. Dr. Tiffany Joseph is an author, professor, and researcher of sociology and anthropology who examines race, immigration, and healthcare access. She is known for her award winning research publications and her books: Race on the Move: Brazilian Migrants and the Global Reconstruction and Not All In: Race, Immigration, and Healthcare Exclusion in the Age of Obamacare. Dr. Joseph is an associate professor of Sociology and International Affairs at Northeastern University and continues to conduct ground-breaking research in intersections between accessibility and healthcare. Joseph currently lives with her husband and two children in Massachusetts. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Imagining a better healthcare system amidst shifting paradigms | Tiffany Joseph | TEDxNortheasternU

description: Ellen explores the rise of factory farming and shares her personal decision to stop eating meat. Her talk shows how individual actions can add up to meaningful change. I (somewhat controversially) decided to stop eating meat at the age of 9. I'm now 17 and have explored this idea in more depth. Much was to be said about my choice by friends and family and even people I had just met, with the most popular question being: "Why?". I felt that I never gave anyone an answer that satisfied both them and me. So here it is. description: Bertie tells anecdotes from his experiences at football grounds across the UK, discusses how fans are being 'priced out', and provides an entertaining talk for his captive audience. I have followed football, especially my beloved Carlisle, since I was born. I’ve travelled across the country to watch matches, visiting 34 of the 92 English clubs. Carlisle  is my true love, something I’m deeply passionate about. Going to games has kept me focused and motivated, because my mum always said if I didn’t work hard, I couldn’t go. It’s helped me cope with exam stress and shaped the person I am today. Through the game, I’ve met great friends like Rhys and ‘Uncle Charlie,’ who has taught me life lessons. I’ve also learned responsibility—once I wasn’t allowed to go to Barrow because I’d been in trouble. None of this would be possible if the price of my passion was a joke.
